title: Understanding Exponential Regularization
text: Exponential regularization uses the function Pow(theta)=lambda*sum{i=1}{p}{10**theta_i}. This means that the penalty increases exponentially with the value of $$\theta_i$$.

title: Comparing with L2 Regularization
text: L2 regularization uses the function lambda*sum{i=1}{p}{theta_i**2}. Consider how the penalty changes for large positive and negative values of $$\theta_i$$ compared to exponential regularization.

title: Comparing with L1 Regularization
text: L1 regularization uses the function lambda*sum{i=1}{p}{abs(theta_i)}. It is known for its ability to perform feature selection by setting some coefficients to zero.

title: Analyzing Statement A
text: Does exponential regularization penalize large positive coefficients more than L2 regularization? Consider the exponential growth of the penalty.

title: Analyzing Statement B
text: Does exponential regularization penalize large negative coefficients more than L2 regularization? Think about how negative values affect the exponential function.

title: Analyzing Statement C
text: Is L2 regularization more effective than exponential regularization when we want parameters close to zero? Consider the nature of the quadratic penalty in L2 regularization.

title: Analyzing Statement D
text: Can exponential regularization be used for feature selection like L1 regularization? Consider the nature of the exponential penalty and its effect on coefficients.
